column1: # Declared exceptions to the shaped patterns in hygiene-patterns.tsv.
# Format: label<TAB>extended-regex, in the SAME dialect the pattern it
# exempts is written in -- POSIX ERE, because `hygiene.sh` applies this
# through `sed -E`, the one tool that shares grep -E's regex flavour, so a
# maintainer reading a pattern and its exception beside it reads one syntax
# rather than two.
# WHAT THIS DOES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. An exception does not loosen or
# rewrite the pattern it names: `hygiene.sh` still runs the pattern's own
# regex, unedited, against the full line. Every occurrence of the exception
# regex is then removed from that line, and the pattern is asked again
# whether anything is LEFT. If nothing is, every hit on the line was
# accounted for by a declared-safe form and the line is clean; if something
# still matches, it is reported exactly as before -- so a line carrying both
# a forge remote AND a private one still fires.
# This is a data-driven carve-out, not a weaker pattern: the shape the
# pattern names is unchanged, and a form not listed here still fires -- a
# login at a DOTTED private host, colon-terminated, is the whole reason
# `ssh-user-at-host` keeps matching after this file exists. (Not a bare,
# dotless hostname: a fresh-instance review of #83 found an earlier example
# here used one and never fired, since the pattern requires a dot --
# pre-existing and unrelated to this file, corrected rather than repeated.
# Not written as a literal instance again, for the same reason this row's
# own regex is not written as the string it exempts.)
# Ruled 2026-09-12 on #72. `ssh-user-at-host` exists to catch a PRIVATE
# remote a captured log carries by accident -- a build box, a personal
# machine -- and a public forge's own SSH remote form is not that: it is the
# same string in every clone of every public repository on that host,
# published by the forge itself. Four forges named here; the shape is one
# alternation, so a fifth is one more name in it, not a new row.
# AND A PACKAGE LOCKFILE'S OWN KEY FORM, by the same argument. pnpm spells a
# resolved package as `name@1.2.3:` (and `name@1.2.3(peer@4.5.6)` inside a
# peer suffix), which the pattern reads as a login at a dotted host. A dotted
# all-numeric "host" with exactly three parts, terminated by `:`, `(`, `)`
# or `'`, is a semver in a lockfile and is not a hostname at all -- it is the
# same string in every install from the same registry. The terminator is
# part of the exception on purpose: an IPv4 has a fourth part after its third
# dot, so a login at a private address is left exactly as it was and still
# fires. (No literal instance of either form is written here, per the rule
# above.)
# Added 2026-09-20 with the first JavaScript package (`exercise/`); disclosed
# on that PR as an edit outside its directory.
ssh-user-at-host
